question: The Prysmian Group, a leader in the field of energy and telecommunications cables and systems, has announced the closure of the FOS fibre-optic production plant in Battipaglia, Salerno. The plant, which employs around 340 workers, is an important technological resource for Italy and the EU as a whole.

The decision was influenced by high energy costs and adverse global market conditions, compounded by unfair competition from non-EU countries with lower production costs, lower quality and less stringent regulations. This scenario is a threat to EU industry, technological innovation and job security.

It is imperative that urgent action be taken to support the EU companies and workers affected, by determining support measures that are effective and accessible. Unfair competition from outside the EU needs to be addressed, with consideration given to customs duties or other trade protections in order to balance market conditions. In the light of the above: 1.
What immediate action will the Commission take to provide concrete support to the EU companies and workers affected by the closure of production plants such as Prysmian Group’s?
How does it plan to tackle the unfair competition from non-EU countries that is threatening EU industry?
What initiatives are under way to mitigate the impact of energy costs on energy-intensive industries in the EU and ensure their global competitiveness?
answer: Dealing with plant restructurings is primarily a Member State competence.

Several Directives (1) stipulate minimum requirements for the protection of workers. The Commission also calls on Member States to support the implementation of the Quality Framework for Restructuring (2) through appropriate means.

In the event of dismissals, the European Globalisation Adjustment Fund for Displaced Workers (EGF) (3) may intervene if the Member State applies and the criteria defined in the regulation are fulfilled. Workers may be eligible to receive support for skills development and job search under the European Social Fund Plus (4), as well. 2.

The Commission aims for a level playing field to ensure fair competition, the competitiveness of EU industry and to protect jobs. The enforcement of trade defence measures is a priority for the Commission. In 2021 the Commission imposed anti-dumping duties on imports of optical fibre cables from China and is currently conducting an anti-dumping investigation on imports of optical fibre cables from India (5).
The EU has recently expanded its regulatory toolbox with further measures to ensure a level playing field for all companies active on the Single Market (6).

3. The energy transition offers a chance to boost competitiveness and phase-out dependence on fossil fuels imports from unreliable partners. The Commission has tackled the energy price crisis including through emergency measures, some of them prolonged, in order to avoid extraordinarily high gas prices with a dynamic price cap — the Market Correction Mechanism.
The Net-Zero Industry Act (7) will also support decarbonisation projects of energy intensive industries and avoid creating new dependencies on clean technologies.
